title: What is known about 1RB0LA_0RC0RF_0RD0RA_1LD0LE_0LA1LE_---1LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LA_0RC0RF_0RD0RA_1LD0LE_0LA1LE_---1LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. It is a close relative of 1RB0LA_0RC---_0RD0RF_1LD0LE_0LA1LE_0RA0LA: the tape is blocks of 1s separated by single 0s, and each round turns the first block into 0 1 pairs that come back as gliders, each moving a hole 3 cells left. Rounds from a first block of even length are step for step the same as in that machine and are proved in Lean; rounds from an odd block differ, and that is also where a halt could happen.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the whole round from an even first block and no halt in the first 107 steps. The machine halts exactly when F reads a 0; F is entered only from B reading a 1, and on the tapes seen that happens when a sweep that has passed an odd block meets a block of a single 1 (C>1 0 1 0 runs into F on a 0). In 109 steps no round after step 2,136 started with a block shorter than 12 cells.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: The pieces of a round
claims.text: The same statements as for 1RB0LA_0RC---_0RD0RF_1LD0LE_0LA1LE_0RA0LA, proved for this machine: the sweep 0 C> (11)^n → (01)^n 0 C> (here by B, C and A), the glider 0 0 D> 1^n → 1^n 0 0 D>, the glider cycle and the first and last pieces of a round.

claims.title: Rounds from an even first block
claims.text: E> 0 1^(4k+4) 0 1^(a+3) 0 1 R reaches E> 0 1^(a+k+4) 0 1^(3k+7) R and E> 0 1^(4k+6) 0 1^(a+4) 0 1 R reaches E> 0 1^(a+k+5) 0 1^(3k+10) R, for all k, a, R: [4K, a, b, …] → [a+K, 3K+3+b, …] and [4K+2, a, b, …] → [a+K, 3K+6+b, …].

claims.title: Where the two machines part
claims.text: The sweep crossing a hole after an odd stretch, C>1 0 1 1 → 0 1 0 C>1, is the same in both machines; on C>1 0 1 0 (a block of one 1 after the hole) this machine reaches F on a 0 and halts, where the twin carries on.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 3,867 cells have been visited and 3,172 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 3.34·10<sup>11</sup> steps (accelerated run)
claims.text: The run-length simulator tools/py/bbtools/rleaccel.py (blocks of 2 cells, runs crossed in one step, and cycle jumps, each used only after its one-cycle rule has been proved symbolically for all lengths; tested cell for cell against direct runs) runs 194,600,000 macro steps from blank tape without a halt. That is more than 3.34·1011 machine steps; the tape then spans 26,988 cells.

claims.title: Every round starts on single holes
claims.text: At the 660 times up to step 10<sup>9</sup> that the head is at the left end in state E on a 0, the tape is blocks of 1s separated by single 0s (except at steps 7 and 204): 2 blocks 593 times, 3 blocks 53, 4 blocks 10, 5 blocks 2. The shortest block at a round start is 3 (step 1,605); after step 2,136 it is never below 12.

claims.title: The even rounds follow the formula
claims.text: All 329 rounds from an even first block in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps follow [a+K, 3K+3+b, …] (x = 4K) or [a+K, 3K+6+b, …] (x = 4K+2).

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.331). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.332).

claims.title: Why the width grows like t<sup>1/3</sup>
claims.text: As in the twin: about x/4 gliders each cross the second block and come back, so a round costs about 1.5·x·a ~ w<sup>2</sup> steps, and it adds 3 ones (x = 4K), 4 (x = 4K+2) or 4 to 28 (odd x). So w<sup>3</sup> ~ t.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The even rounds are proved; odd first blocks make the sweep pass through holes, and the machine would halt if such a sweep met a block of a single 1. A proof needs the odd rounds as rules and an invariant that keeps blocks long.

check: gcc -O2 -o tmrun tools/c/tmrun.c && ./tmrun 1RB0LA_0RC0RF_0RD0RA_1LD0LE_0LA1LE_---1LB 1000000000 at E L 100000 > el.txt && python3 holdouts/1RB0LA_0RC0RF_0RD0RA_1LD0LE_0LA1LE_---1LB/py/rounds.py el.txt

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Like its twin 1RB0LA_0RC---…, this machine keeps a nearly solid block of 1s with one or two holes, and each round moves a hole: the first block becomes 0 1 pairs, and every two pairs come back as a glider that knocks the hole 3 cells left. Rounds cost about the square of the width and add a few cells, so the width grows like the cube root of the time.

facts.text: A round from a first block of length 4k+4 or 4k+6 is proved for all k and all second blocks.
Even rounds in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps that follow the proved formula.
Width after t steps: a round costs about w<sup>2</sup> steps and adds 3 to 28 ones.

sections.heading: Same rounds as its twin
html: Stop the machine whenever the head is at the left end in state E. The tape is then a few blocks of 1s separated by single 0s: at step 997,741,851 it is E>0 1^3127 0 1^726, blocks [3127, 726].

A round does what it does in 1RB0LA_0RC---_0RD0RF_1LD0LE_0LA1LE_0RA0LA. The sweep turns the first block's pairs 1 1 into 0 1 (here with states B, C, A instead of B, C, F, A). A first block of even length ends the sweep with a glider, two 0s that move right through the next block at one cell per 5 steps. Each glider reaches the next hole, fills it, and leaves a hole 3 cells further left; E walks back, two more pairs make the next glider, and so on. The round from [16, 20] is identical, step for step, in both machines and ends at [24, 15] after 715 steps.
Lean proves the whole round for every even first block: [4K, a, b, …] becomes [a+K, 3K+3+b, …] and [4K+2, a, b, …] becomes [a+K, 3K+6+b, …]. All 329 even rounds of the first 109 steps match.

sections.heading: Odd blocks, and a halt on a block of one
html: When the first block is odd, the sweep runs through the hole into the next block (C>1 0 1 1 becomes 0 1 0 C>1), leaving a mark behind. Here the two machines differ: in this one, if the stretch after the hole is a single 1 (C>1 0 1 0), the next steps put F on a 0, which is the halting transition. So the machine halts if a sweep coming out of an odd block ever meets a block of length 1.

Blocks at round starts are long: after step 2,136, none is shorter than 12 cells in 109 steps. Whether short blocks can appear in the middle of a round, where the gliders rework the tape, is part of the open question.

sections.heading: Why the width grows like t<sup>1/3</sup>
html: Each glider crosses the second block and E walks back over it, so a round from blocks [x, a] costs about 1.5·x·a steps, of the order of the width squared, and adds only a few ones (3 to 28). A constant gain per w2 steps gives w3 ~ t. After 109 steps the tape is 3,867 cells wide.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.331). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.332).
After 109 steps the tape spans 3,867 cells (1,355 left of the start, 1,822 right), with a density of 1s of 0.82.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A twin of 1RB0LA_0RC---_0RD0RF_1LD0LE_0LA1LE_0RA0LA: blocks of 1s with single holes, rounds of sweep and gliders that move a hole 3 cells at a time; the even rounds are the same and proved in Lean, the odd ones differ and can halt on a block of length 1.
